record.paper_title: New Open Problems Related to Old Conjectures by Helleseth
record.context_brief: Avoid elliptic-curve proof for the q−2 case
record.original_question: Take p ∈ {2, 3} and let L be a finite field of characteristic p and order q. For the exponent s = q − 2, which satisfies s ≡ 1 (mod p − 1) exactly in these two characteristics, can one prove the Helleseth Vanishing Conjecture for this case without using the theory of elliptic curves? In other words, can one show by a different method that there exists a nonzero a ∈ L such that W_{L,q−2}(a) = 0?

evidence.quote: Problem 1.2. Prove the Helleseth Vanishing Conjecture for p ∈ {2, 3} and s = q − 2 without using of the theory of elliptic curves.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $p\in\{2,3\}$ be a prime and let $L=\mathbb{F}_q$ be a finite field of characteristic $p$ with $q=p^m$ elements. Fix a nontrivial additive character $\chi\colon L\to\mathbb{C}^\times$ (for instance $\chi(x)=\exp(2\pi i\,\mathrm{Tr}_{L/\mathbb{F}_p}(x)/p)$). For an integer $s$ coprime to $q-1$ and $a\in L$, define the Walsh (cross-correlation) transform
$$W_{L,s}(a)\;=\;\sum_{x\in L}\chi\!\left(x^{s}-a x\right).$$
Take the exponent $s=q-2$ (note $q-2\equiv 1\pmod{p-1}$ exactly when $p\in\{2,3\}$). The Helleseth Vanishing Conjecture asserts that there exists a nonzero $a\in L$ with $W_{L,s}(a)=0$.

Prove that for $p\in\{2,3\}$ and $s=q-2$ there exists a nonzero $a\in L$ such that $W_{L,q-2}(a)=0$, by a method that does not invoke the theory of elliptic curves over finite fields.
artifact.status_search_result: No web evidence was found of an elementary (non-elliptic-curve) proof of the Helleseth Vanishing Conjecture for the case $p\in\{2,3\}$, $s=q-2$. The known proof uses point counting on elliptic curves; the request for an alternative proof appears to remain open.
